manuscripts.title: A Packing of 5 Four-Spaces in R9
manuscripts.abstract: We give 5 4-dimensional subspaces of R^9 whose smallest squared chordal distance is at least 2.777625. This cell of the table of best Grassmannian packings has no published value. The best value implied by known packings is 2.666497, obtained by deleting 1 of the 6 four-spaces of the packing found by this search. The value is checked with exact rational arithmetic from integer coordinates. We do not claim it is optimal.

This cell of the table of best Grassmannian packings has no published value. The best value implied by known packings is 0.842330, obtained by deleting 1 of the 87 lines of the packing found by this search. The value is checked with exact rational arithmetic from integer coordinates. We do not claim it is optimal.

This cell of the table of best Grassmannian packings has no published value. The best value implied by known packings is 2.124575, obtained by deleting 1 of the 87 three-spaces of the packing found by this search. The value is checked with exact rational arithmetic from integer coordinates. We do not claim it is optimal.

manuscripts.title: Spreading 32 Points in the Plane
manuscripts.abstract: We place 32 points in the plane so that the squared ratio of the largest to the smallest distance between them is at most 29.22375+. Erich Friedman's table of best known configurations lists n up to 31. Deleting a point from our 33-point configuration gives 29.80601; this one is smaller. The ratio is computed exactly from the published coordinates. We do not claim it is optimal.

Erich Friedman's table of best known configurations lists n up to 31. Deleting a point from our 36-point configuration gives 32.83385; this one is smaller. The ratio is computed exactly from the published coordinates. We do not claim it is optimal.
